subject: Human Evolution
title: Sitting Disease
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sitting Disease.

hook.text: Humans evolved to walk 10–15 km daily. The average office worker sits for 10 hours and walks under 1 km.

buildup.text: Prolonged sitting weakens glutes, tightens hip flexors, and compresses spinal discs—all bipedal structures.

discovery.text: Research links sitting over 8 hours daily to heart disease, diabetes, and early death—even with exercise.

twist.text: Our hunter-gatherer ancestors rested by squatting, which keeps muscles active. Chairs bypass that.

climax.text: The body built for walking breaks down when it's parked in chairs all day. We misuse what evolution gave us.

punchline.text: The chair is bipedalism's worst enemy.

quiz.question: Why is prolonged sitting harmful for bipedal bodies?
options: It weakens the muscles and structures evolved for walking
